message.content: {"B_expression":"-1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))**2)","C_expression":"0","derivation":"Retain the inherited source-only construction unchanged. The generation-1 numerical feedback confirms the design: for every APPLIED point within chi_r*chi_u support, the pure remainder (2g+g^2-r) is exactly 0.0 at double precision, while the whole residual E equals the cross term 2*u*g to within 1e-8 to 1e-9. For example, UNIFORM:t=1/64:x=1/8:s=0 has pure=0.0, cross=-2.038e-8, residual=-1.99e-8. The B correction r^2*B = -r^2/(2(1+sqrt(1+r))^2) cancels the O(r^2) pure remainder identically (verified by the quadratic identity in the W0 derivation). Adding a C term would shift g by delta_g = u*r*C, introducing a new pure remainder ~2*u*r*C of the same order as the cross term it would reduce, yielding no net improvement in E. The W0 draft's proposed C=-1/2+r/(2(1+sqrt(1+r))^2) was correctly rejected on this ground: it double-counts the structural 2*u*g coupling. Smoothness: B is C-infinity for r>-1; on the outer rectangle |r|<=1/2 we have 1+r>=1/2>0, so sqrt(1+r)>=sqrt(1/2) and the denominator 2*(1+sqrt(1+r))^2 >= 2*(1+sqrt(1/2))^2 > 0. C=0 is trivially smooth. Both bodies are smooth on an open neighborhood of the closed rectangle [-1/2,1/2]x[-1/4,1/4].","inspect":[{"file_id":"CALC/draft.json","limit":4096,"offset":0}],"note":"Successor should verify: (1) the next target increment p2=p1+tau^3*k2 produces r of order tau^3~5e-7, at which r^2*B~1e-13 is below double-precision noise and the program effectively reduces to g=r/2; (2) if any point develops |u| in the transition zone (1/8<|u|<1/4) where chi_u is partially active, the chi_u smooth step modulates the B and C contributions continuously; (3) for |u|>=1/4 points (LEFT/RIGHT edge families with large z deviations), chi_u=0 and only r/2 is applied regardless of B,C values; (4) the residual floor at current scale is O(u*r) from the structural cross term, not a defect of the coefficient; (5) retain this program unless the field develops a systematic u-dependent bias across multiple stages that the cross term alone cannot explain."}
